Mr. A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J: The petitioner obtained this Rule upon an application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act read with section 151 C.P.C. for condonation of delay in filing First Appeal (F.A.T. No. 319 of 1991) in this Division. 

 Mr. Md. Harun-or-Rashid on May 15, 1991 for filing the appeal. The learned Advocate Mr. Md. Harun-or-Rashid received those paper on the following day and he wanted to know about the grounds for condonation of delay and asked money for filing the appeal which was not supplied to him. The petitioner furnished the grounds for condonation of delay on May 21, 1991 and after taking necessary steps the appeal was filed on May 25, 1991. Thus the appeal was filed out of time by 67 days. The petitioner further stated that the appellant was misguided by the learned Advocate to whom the papers were initially sent for filing the appeal. In these circumstances the delay occurred and is barred by limitation. The delay is unintentional and was due to no laches on the part of the petitioner. 

 6. Mr. Akram Hussain Amin at the outset opposes the rule on the ground of limitation placing reliance on the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 which is a special law and section 7(1) of the Act prescribes a special period of limitation for filing the appeal in the High Court Division. According to sub-section (1) of section 7 the appeal is to be filed within 30 days from the date of the judgment and decree. Sub-section (2) of section 7 also enjoins upon the appellant to deposit 50% of the decretal amount in the trial court before filing the appeal. He submits that the Act which is a special law the period of limitation prescribed therein shall be strictly construed and section 5 of the Limitation Act does not apply for condonation of delay in filing the present appeal. He submits that like the Special Powers Act, 1974 the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 is also a special law and similarly section 5 of the Limitation Act has not been made applicable to this Act for condonation of delay in filing the appeal. Mr. Harun-or-Rashid appearing for the petitioner submits that section 5 is applicable in this case. He cites the decision in the case of Ishaque and others Vs. The Government of Bangladesh, 43 DLR(AD)28. He referred us to paragraph-7, 17 and 36 to contend that although the act provides a special period of limitation the appeal can be entertained after expiry of that period. A close reading of the said decision indicates that the contention of Mr. Rashid is of no substance in that the facts of that case was quite distinguishable from the facts of this case and the principle laid down therein relates to arbitration case under East Bengal Emergency Requisition Act. 1948 and the rule framed thereunder. In that case the majority opinion of the A.D. is that the appellate court is not empowered to condone the delay in filing the appeal out of time under section 5 of the Limitation Act by reason of section-29(2) of the Limitation Act which prescribes a different period of limitation from the period prescribed by the First Schedule of the Limitation Act, 1908. It further held in that in a case where 'an order appealed against is a nulity the statute of limitation will not apply and the appeal can be entertained beyond the period of limitation. In the case before us the petitioner's case is not of a nulity of the decree. Therefore the principle enunciated in the said case does not apply here. Mr. Harun or Rashid also referred to us the decision in the case of Ahsan Ali and others Vs. District Judge and Settlement Commissioner Sukkur and others, 21 DLR (SC) 139 to contend that time barred appeal can be entertained after expiry of period of limitation prescribed in the special law on condonation the delay in filing the appeal under section 5 of the Limitation Act. In that case it was found that the Revision and the appeal before the Additional Settlement Commissioner and the District Judge who was the ex-officio Settlement Officer was entertained after the period of limitation expired. That was a case under Displaced Person (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act. The learned Chief Justice while delivering the judgment found that the Act by section 19(3) section 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1980 were made applicable for computation of period or on limitation of 15 days as provided in section 19(2) of the said Act. It was further observed that although no application for condonation of delay was filed the court can condone the delay on the evidence to be laid by the parties it supports of their respective cases. Thus we are also of the opinion that this decision does not help the petitioner as in the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 the Ss. 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act have not been made applicable under any provision of Artha Rin Adalat Act. 1990. Mr. Amin also contends that the opposite party had already satisfied the decree and as such the appeal has become infructuous. The instant appeal is against the dismissal of the suit relating to Tk. 6,44,736/- out of total claim of Tk.8,02,230/-. We do not understand how this appeal has become infructuous due to payment of decretal amount where an appeal is maintainable against the dismissal as a whole from a decree passed in part in the suit. In the instant case the appellant certainly has right to appeal against the decree appealed. The contention of Mr. Amin accordingly on this court failed. Mr. Rashid, however, argues, on merit of this Rule, that due to misguidance of the learned Advocate to whom the paper was given initially for filing the appeal the appeal become barred by limitation and the petitioner has no laches and there was no negligence in prosecuting with the appeal on the part of the petitioner. It appears from the petition that the petitioner did not disclose the name of the learned Advocate to whom the file was sent and accordingly we direct to disclose the name of the petitioner and the petitioner discloses the name by filing supplementary affidavit. The affidavit was sworn by Mr. Z.I. Khan, an Advocate of this Court who stated that due to want of experience on his part the mistake in computing the period of limitation occurred which was a bonafide mistake and he prayed for condonation of delay for such mistake. We found that the statement of the learned Advocate is bonafide. But the question remains whether the delay can be condoned where application section 5 of the Limitation Act has no role to play. On this we have expressed our view earlier. Therefore the rule is not also maintainable and fails for non-application of section 5 of the limitation Act to Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990. 

 7. Mr. Rashid also drew our attention to the judgment delivered by us in Civil Rule No. 88(F) of 1991 on 15.11.1992. In that case we condoned the delay ex parte as no one appeared for the opposite-party and no objection was raised on limitation as is now seriously contended by the opposite-party, subject to objection to be raised at the time of hearing of the appeal in the judgment pronounced in Civil Rule No.88 (F) of 1991 by us we did not express our final and a 

 complete opinion on limitation as we have kept the point open to be raised by the Respondent at the time of hearing of appeal. Therefore the said opinion cannot be pressed in service by the appellant as the opinion was subject to raising objection by the Respondent and final opinion
